title: SolveResultGeneration
description: CLI-facing twin of ../solve.schema.json, used ONLY for the `claude --json-schema` flag that constrains prompts/claude/v1/solve.md's generation. Deliberately avoids $ref/$defs, oneOf/anyOf/allOf, const, minLength/maxLength/minItems/maxItems, and nullable ('type': [...]) fields -- Anthropic's structured-output / tool-schema support does not cover all of JSON Schema, and a few of these constructs (oneOf and $ref especially) have been reported to make Claude Code's schema handling fail outright rather than degrade gracefully. Length/count limits that lived in 'minLength' etc. here are conveyed as description text instead -- the model treats them as guidance, and the real enforcement is downstream: prompts/claude/v1/compress.md's hard limits plus the render QA gate's overflow check (src/rendering/render.py). The FULL, precise shape (oneOf-discriminated diagrams, $ref-shared cell/pointer definitions, exact length/count bounds) is still enforced after generation by src/claude/validator.py's validate_schema() against ../solve.schema.json using the Python jsonschema library, which has no such restrictions. See ARCHITECTURE.md 'Why two schema files per stage'.

diagrams.description: 0-2 items from the diagram library (see the prompt's 'Diagram library' section). Omit this key entirely, or leave it an empty array, when no diagram genuinely fits -- never force one. Each item is EITHER an array_pointers diagram (populate 'cells', and optionally 'title'/'pointers'/'caption'/'result' -- leave 'cases' unset) OR a comparison_states diagram (populate 'cases' -- leave 'title'/'cells'/'pointers'/'caption'/'result' at the top level of the item unset). Never mix fields from both shapes in the same item.

component.description: Selects which of the two diagram shapes this item uses.

cells.description: array_pointers only. 1-14 items, each {value, state}. state is one of neutral/highlight/invalid/muted (default neutral). value is max 12 chars.

pointers.description: array_pointers only. Up to 4 items, each {index, label}. label max 16 chars.

cases.description: comparison_states only. 2-3 items, each {verdict, label, description, cells, pointers, result}.

cells.description: 1-14 items, each {value, state}, same shape as array_pointers cells.

reasoning_panel.description: Optional 'why this works' callout. Omit this key entirely (do not set it to null) when the correctness argument doesn't compress well into a short bullet list.
